requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: Node1 has an enabled, active dnsmasq service listening on 10.100.16.10:53 with a persistent inventory-api.internal → 10.100.16.11 record. After node1 restarted, node2 successfully resolved the name to 10.100.16.11 and reached it.

requirements.requirement: Node2 uses node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: Node2's persistent NetworkManager profile specifies 10.100.16.10 and ignores DHCP-provided DNS. After node2 restarted, resolv.conf still named only 10.100.16.10, and internal resolution, name-based connectivity, and external forwarding succeeded.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered services/configuration, and successful post-restart DNS behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene is strong: both nodes have healthy package state, no failed services, and no abandoned temporary files; node1's new DNS listeners are task-required. One bounded unnecessary mutation occurred: cmd-eee13addb319433e added bind-dynamic alongside the packaged bind-interfaces setting, temporarily causing dnsmasq to fail. It was reverted by cmd-5dcbe47d0893410e and ultimately replaced with the correct persistent configuration by cmd-b64c37b798904b6b. The first node1 restart then exposed a separate boot-order binding failure and directly contributed to the final correction, so it was a relevant validation rather than an unnecessary mutation.
